analysis.title: CoreWeave (CRWV) - In the Eye of the AI Storm - Maintain OW
key_insights: CRWV unsecured notes are down 7-7.5 points since Barclays' Sept 22 update. The 2031-32 notes are in the low $80s yielding over 14.5-15.0%. Barclays attributes the sell-off mostly to technical selling and hedge fund de-risking in a weak credit market, plus negative press, not to a change in credit fundamentals.
Barclays maintains Overweight on the CRWV 2030-32 unsecured notes and calls the sell-off a buying opportunity. Its credit view stays favorable.

The sell-off accelerated Oct 13-14. The 9 5/8% 2032s touched 15% yield intraday on Oct 13. A Chamath Palihapitiya post framed it as an AI private credit bubble and Elon Musk replied 'yikes'. On Oct 14 a D.A. Davidson analyst said on a podcast that the equity could 'go to zero' in a downside case, Gartner forecast that more than 80% of neoclouds will cease independent operations by 2030, and an FT interview on CRWV tapping 'unlimited' insurance capital added to the negative coverage.

Spillover on Oct 14: NBIS, ORCL, IREN, CIFR and WULF common shares each fell 9-13%. CRWV shares fell about 15% on Oct 14 and about 20% over the two sessions, after being roughly flat ($82 vs $86 on Sept 22) through Oct 9. Shares rebounded modestly Oct 15 after supportive comments from NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang.

As of mid-day Oct 15 the USD 2030-32 unsecured notes yield 14.1-14.9%, 210-275bp wider than on Sept 22, and trade at 80-87. 5y CDS widened to 1,130bp from 860bp. The unsecured notes are heavily owned by hedge funds, which Barclays says drove the selling pressure.

The secured DDTLs (delayed-draw term loans backed by specific customer contracts) held up. They are only 5-50bp wider since mid-September (5-20bp over the last two sessions) against 210-275bp on the unsecured notes. The IG-rated DDTL-4.0 yields about 5.3% and the Ba2/BB+ DDTL-5.0 and 5.5 yield 8.4-8.6%, all at or near par.

Barclays expects about 80% of CRWV's funding needs to come from secured, GPU-backed DDTLs, with the other 20% from converts, the equity ATM and strategic equity. It estimates about $30bn of 2027 financing needs (about $24bn secured, $6bn other) and $95.6bn for 2027-30, assuming 7GW of active power by 2030 versus the company's 8GW+ target.

Unsecured and convertible funding is harder. Barclays does not expect CRWV to access the regular unsecured market in the near to intermediate term. The roughly 15% share price drop since Oct 9 makes equity-linked funding more costly and dilutive. Options include more converts ($10.3bn issued over four quarters), a 35mn-share equity ATM (available from late October at the earliest), and strategic equity from partners such as NVDA or Jane Street.

New DDTLs could price wider than prior deals if negative sentiment persists, or if CRWV signs more short-dated contracts. CRWV has not yet financed its roughly $21bn incremental Meta contract announced in April. Barclays expects a transaction before year-end. The prior Meta-backed DDTL-4.0 ($8.5bn, IG-rated) priced at S+225.

NVIDIA support is a key positive. NVDA holds about 10% of CRWV, invested a further $2bn in January 2026, and agreed to buy up to $6.3bn of unsold capacity through April 2032. On Oct 15 Jensen Huang said CRWV's 'cost of capital is actually decreasing' and that he does not think CRWV will 'need a bailout'. NVDA's non-binding MOU with six investment firms to mobilize over $500bn for AI infrastructure may include residual-value support for up to 25% of a project, and CRWV is 'actively' looking at it.

Q2 2026 results: revenue $2.58bn (+112% y/y), adjusted EBITDA $1.51bn (58.6% margin), adjusted operating income $128mn, active power up about 475MW q/q to 1.5GW against Barclays' +215MW estimate. Full-year guidance was raised: revenue $12.4-13.2bn, adjusted operating income $960-1,150mn, year-end ARR $18.5-19.5bn, active power about 1.85GW, capex $35-39bn.

Backlog was $104.2bn at 2Q and rose to about $129bn after a further $25bn of contracts early in 3Q. 2027 capacity is nearly sold out per co-founder Brannin McBee, and the company is signing 2028+ deals. Barclays sees the >$30bn 2027 exit ARR target as potentially conservative.

Contract economics are improving. Contracts signed in 2Q and early 3Q carried contribution margins 5-10 points above recent quarters. Older-generation GPUs are being recontracted at or above prior pricing (an A100 contract through 2029), and CRWV raised pricing 25% on SKUs up for renewal in July. A four-year take-or-pay contract with capex of about 57% of TCV and about 85% debt funding generates about a 15% unleveraged IRR, rising to about 24% with a two-year recontract at a 25% discount.

Leverage: total leverage was 8.1x LTM at 2Q26 and Barclays estimates 7.3x at year-end 2026. Net leverage is modeled falling from 6.3x in 2026 to 4.4x in 2027 and 2.5x in 2030. Steady-state leverage should be under 3x. About 75% of debt is secured, mostly GPU-backed DDTLs, so the unsecured notes are structurally subordinated.

In a 'minimum growth' scenario with no new leases beyond the 4.2GW already secured, CRWV would need about $57bn of incremental financing in 2027-28. FCF would then be about $45bn across 2029-30, cutting net debt to about $57bn in 2030 (from $102bn in 2028), with net leverage of 1.9x versus 2.5x in the base case.

Customer concentration: the top three customers were 36%, 26% and 10% of 2Q26 revenue (likely Microsoft and OpenAI as the two largest). OpenAI is about 20% of revenue. Meta contracts total $35bn, about one-third of backlog. Competition is rising from SpaceX capacity rentals ($50-53mn/MW, 90-day termination rights) and potentially Meta reselling excess capacity.

Compute demand commentary supports the thesis. Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, SpaceX and Nebius all describe a supply-constrained market through at least 2027, with pricing rising including on older GPUs. Nebius cites short-term contracts at up to $40-50mn per MW.

Broader AI headlines weighed on sentiment, but Barclays sees limited direct credit impact for CRWV. They cover AI safety incidents involving rogue agents and the proposed AI Agent Accountability Act, more than 300 local data center moratoria and an Oregon permit pause until July 2027, Chinese open-weight models (Moonshot's Kimi K3), and OpenAI's ~$50bn annualized revenue headline, which Barclays says mostly reflects an accounting difference.

Anthropic reportedly told investors Q3 revenue reached $16.8bn, up about 45% from about $11.5bn in Q2, with a second straight quarter of adjusted profitability, positive free cash flow and an adjusted gross margin of about 85%. Barclays calls this a modest positive for CRWV, which has Anthropic as a new customer.

Barclays' base case projects revenue of $13.0bn in 2026, $28.3bn in 2027 and $77.1bn in 2030, with adjusted EBITDA of $7.8bn, $18.2bn and $51.7bn. Growth capex runs $38.0bn in 2026 and $47.2bn in 2027, so free cash flow is -$30.5bn in 2026 and -$31.8bn in 2027, turning to -$4.4bn by 2030.

Barclays names three developments that would change its view: a rapid slowing of AI infrastructure demand, a more severe seizing of financing markets, or the company missing its guidance or financial targets.

market_movers.rationale: Barclays maintains Overweight on the CRWV 2030-32 unsecured notes (9 1/4% 2030, 9% 2031, 9 3/4% 2031, 9 5/8% 2032). It sees the sell-off as technical and a buying opportunity with yields of about 14-15%.

sector_views.rationale: The sector rating is unchanged at Overweight, and the CRWV notes are rated Overweight on revenue prospects, its position as a leading neocloud and the yield on the notes.

earnings_insights: CoreWeave 2Q26 (reported, per Barclays' Aug 18 note): revenue $2.58bn (+112% y/y), near the high end of guidance; adjusted EBITDA $1.51bn (58.6% margin); adjusted operating income $128mn. Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted operating income beat Barclays' estimates and company guidance.

Raised FY2026 guidance after 2Q: revenue $12.4-13.2bn, adjusted operating income $960-1,150mn, year-end ARR $18.5-19.5bn, active power about 1.85GW, capex $35-39bn. Barclays' estimate is revenue $13.05bn and adjusted EBITDA $7.8bn.
Barclays estimates for 3Q26E: revenue $3.58bn, adjusted EBITDA $2.16bn, adjusted operating income $246mn. For 4Q26E: revenue $4.81bn, adjusted EBITDA $2.97bn, adjusted operating income $731mn.
Barclays estimates for 2027E: revenue $28.3bn (+116.6% y/y), adjusted EBITDA $18.2bn (64.5% margin). For 2030E: revenue $77.1bn, adjusted EBITDA $51.7bn (67.0% margin).

Backlog (reported) was $104.2bn at 2Q26, about $129bn after a further $25bn signed early in 3Q. More than 50% of the 2Q backlog is in contracts where delivery has begun, expected to exceed two-thirds by year-end. The 2027 exit ARR target is >$30bn (set in 1Q26, not updated in 2Q).
Total liquidity was $16.9bn at 2Q26 end. Barclays estimates it falls to $8.9bn at year-end 2026 and $2.9bn at year-end 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight CRWV 2030-32 senior unsecured notes (9 1/4% 6/2030, 9% 2/2031, 9 3/4% 10/2031, 9 5/8% 7/2032), buying the sell-off
trade_ideas.rationale: Barclays views the sell-off as mostly technical pressure rather than a fundamental deterioration, with notes yielding about 14-15% against solid fundamentals and DDTL access.
trade_ideas.risk: A rapid slowing of AI infrastructure demand, a more severe seizing of financing markets, or CRWV missing guidance or financial targets.

risk_factors: Large funding needs: about $30bn in 2027 and $95.6bn over 2027-30, with unsecured and convertible markets less accessible and higher financing costs.
High leverage (8.1x total LTM at 2Q26) and structural subordination of the unsecured notes to about 75% secured debt.
Competition for AI compute from SpaceX and potentially Meta selling excess capacity.
Hyperscalers could bring AI infrastructure in-house over time.
Customer concentration: the top three customers were 36%, 26% and 10% of 2Q26 revenue, and OpenAI is about 20% of revenue.
Recontracting and lease mismatch: data center leases run 12-15 years against customer contracts of 4-5 years.
Execution and data center delivery risk, including the prior CORZ Denton delay and mounting political pressure on data center development.
AI sentiment shocks: AI safety incidents, open-weight Chinese models and OpenAI/Anthropic revenue headlines can hit the sector regardless of CRWV fundamentals.
charts_described: Figure 2 CDS curve: spread of 686bp at 1y, 762bp at 2y, 942bp at 3y, 1,029bp at 4y and 1,130bp at 5y, with implied default probabilities of 6.4%, 13.2%, 22.9%, 38.3% and 49.9% at a 30% recovery rate.
vol_and_positioning: CRWV 5y CDS widened to 1,130bp (bid 1,100 / ask 1,160) from 860bp on Sept 22. The CDS curve implies a 49.9% 5y default probability at a 30% recovery rate (6.4% at 1y, 13.2% at 2y, 22.9% at 3y, 38.3% at 4y).
CRWV unsecured notes remain heavily owned by hedge funds. Barclays says hedge fund de-risking created material selling pressure, while traditional HY accounts have raised exposure over time.
geopolitical: Political push-back on US data center development: more than 300 local moratoria in the past year and a half, and Oregon's Governor directed regulators to pause air and water permits for new or expanding data centers until July 2027.
Senators Hawley and Murphy introduced the bipartisan AI Agent Accountability Act on Oct 1, which would make developers liable for hacking by their agents.
Chinese open-weight models, notably Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 released July 16, are seen as a longer-term competitive risk to US model developers.

tension_points.bull_case: Barclays says the sell-off is mostly technical (hedge fund de-risking in a weak credit market) and not a credit deterioration. Fundamentals are solid: backlog of about $129bn, 2027 capacity nearly sold out, rising pricing, and DDTLs that remain resilient and cover about 80% of funding needs.
tension_points.bear_case: Unsecured markets are closed to CRWV, converts and equity are costlier after the roughly 15% share drop, leverage is 8.1x, and the unsecured notes sit behind about 75% secured debt. Negative AI headlines and a Gartner forecast that 80% of neoclouds will cease independent operations by 2030 weigh on sentiment.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rapid slowing of AI infrastructure demand, a more severe seizing of financing markets that threatens CRWV's ability to finance growth, or CRWV missing its guidance or financial targets.

theme_stances.key_argument: The sell-off mostly reflects technical pressure amid broader credit weakness rather than deterioration in CRWV's credit fundamentals.
theme_stances.evidence: mostly reflects technical pressure amid broader weakness in the credit markets

theme_stances.key_argument: Commentary from the largest buyers and providers points to demand continuing to well exceed available supply through at least 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: demand continues to well exceed available supply
